title: Buying or checking an insurance policy

items.title: The cover amount is stated
items.look_for: The sum insured and whether it is per person or shared
items.why_it_matters: A shared cover can run out on the first claim in a family
items.question_to_ask: Is this cover per person or shared across everyone named?

items.title: The premium and policy period are stated
items.look_for: Premium amount, how often it is paid and the policy dates
items.question_to_ask: When is the premium due and what is the grace period?

items.title: Waiting periods are listed
items.look_for: Initial waiting period and any condition-specific waiting periods
items.why_it_matters: A claim inside a waiting period is normally refused
items.question_to_ask: Which conditions have a waiting period, and how long?

items.title: Pre-existing conditions are addressed
items.look_for: How declared conditions are treated and after how long they are covered
items.why_it_matters: Non-disclosure is the most common reason a claim is rejected
items.question_to_ask: What must I declare, and when will declared conditions be covered?

items.title: The exclusions are listed
items.look_for: Treatments, causes or situations the policy does not cover
items.why_it_matters: Exclusions decide what you are actually buying

items.title: Any caps within the cover are stated
items.look_for: Room rent caps, per-procedure caps and co-payment percentages
items.why_it_matters: Caps can leave you paying a large share even within the cover
items.question_to_ask: Is there a room rent limit or a co-payment?

items.title: How to claim is explained
items.look_for: Cashless and reimbursement steps, and who to notify
items.why_it_matters: Missing a step can cost you the claim
items.question_to_ask: What do I have to do, and by when, to make a claim?

items.title: Claim notification deadlines are stated
items.look_for: How many hours or days you have to inform the insurer
items.why_it_matters: Late notification is a common ground for rejection
items.question_to_ask: How quickly must I inform you after an admission?

items.title: Where cashless treatment works is stated
items.look_for: A reference to a network list and how to check it
items.why_it_matters: Outside the network you pay first and claim later
items.question_to_ask: How do I check whether a hospital is in the network?

items.title: Renewal terms are stated
items.look_for: Whether renewal is guaranteed and how the premium may change
items.why_it_matters: A policy you cannot renew is only useful for one year
items.question_to_ask: Can the policy be refused at renewal, and how can the premium change?

items.title: The free-look period is stated
items.look_for: A period within which you can cancel and get the premium back
items.why_it_matters: It is your only chance to withdraw without cost
items.question_to_ask: How long do I have to cancel if I change my mind?

items.title: A grievance and ombudsman route is given
items.look_for: A grievance officer and a reference to the insurance ombudsman
items.why_it_matters: It is the escalation path if a claim is refused
items.question_to_ask: Who do I escalate to if a claim is rejected?

suggested_questions: What is not covered by this policy?
How long are the waiting periods?
Is there a room rent limit or a co-payment?
How quickly do I have to inform the insurer about a claim?
Can the policy be refused at renewal?

scenarios.title: I make a claim in the first year
A condition I did not mention comes up
I am treated at a hospital outside the network

facts_to_have_ready: The policy number and the dates it runs between
Who is covered under the policy
The date of the treatment or event you are claiming for
What you told the insurer when you bought the policy
documents_to_bring: The policy document and the schedule
The proposal form you filled in
Hospital bills and discharge summary, if claiming
